courses.subject: SOSC
courses.title: Social Innovation Around the World
courses.description:
This course adopts an applied, comparative, interdisciplinary, and experiential approach to understanding how social sciences are applied innovatively to address real problems in different cultural, political, and economic contexts. Rather than studying theories in the abstract, students examine how evidence‑based innovations are adapted on the ground by local organizations. The focus is on translation of theory to practice, contextual sensitivity, and comparative learning that sharpens judgment about what works, where, and why.

This course is designed based on the following principles:
• Global competence with local relevance: Students learn to read a problem through multiple cultural lenses, then apply those lessons back to Hong Kong, which will be a critical skill for social innovation.
• Evidence‑to‑action mindset: By observing working innovations and talking with practitioners, students see how data, design, and community realities meet, improving their ability to evaluate and adapt solutions rather than copy‑and‑paste them.
• Experiential learning: Unlike most courses that rely solely on case readings or simulations, this course brings students abroad for structured field study during which they can learn from local experts, visit local practitioners, and interview local people on social science topics.
• Problem focus: Each cohort explores a single theme in one locale, then translates those insights into an interdisciplinary innovation tailored to Hong Kong. It bridges global learning with local action.
• Professional readiness: The course strengthens field research skills (interviewing, observation, rapid synthesis) and communication. These competencies are highly valued by their future employers.
• Ethical and contextual judgment: Exposure to diverse institutions and social norms builds cultural inclusion and sharper ethical reasoning about implementation trade‑offs.
courses.learning_outcomes:
Students who complete this course are expected to be able to

1. Compare and interpret how social science frameworks are applied across contexts by analyzing how different disciplines conceptualize and address the course theme in Hong Kong and the destination country, identifying similarities, differences, and underlying institutional or cultural assumptions.
2. Conduct structured field-based inquiry during the overseas study by engaging professionally with experts and practitioners, applying basic qualitative methods (e.g., systematic observation, interviewing, fieldnote documentation), and synthesizing first-hand evidence into coherent analytical insights.
3. Critically evaluate observed social innovations by assessing their problem definition, implementation design, empirical support, ethical considerations, and contextual constraints, and by explaining why they succeed or encounter limitations in specific environments.
4. Translate global learning into locally relevant proposals by identifying which elements of an innovation are transferable to Hong Kong, what contextual adaptations are necessary, and how interdisciplinary knowledge can inform feasible, evidence-based solutions.

• There will be a theme for each trip. All the seminars and site visits are arranged around this theme, from various aspects of social science. For example:

- Well-being and mental health

- Sustainability and environmental challenges

- Ageing

- AI & Smart City

- Inequality

- Housing & Homelessness

- Community Safety

• Students are required to write a report after the trip that covers:

- What they learned from the trip.

- Design an interdisciplinary social innovation for similar problems in Hong Kong, inspired by the local applications.

courses.subject: SOSC
courses.title: AI for Social Science Research
courses.description: The course is designed to equip students with foundational knowledge and practical insights into the role of generative artificial intelligence (AI) in social science research, with a particular focus on applied social science research in frontier technology sectors, policy areas, and decision-making processes for leaders in the public, non-governmental, and private sectors. Course participants will learn and discuss applications, strengths, and limitations of generative AI in the social sciences, including public policy and management, social innovation, and sustainability for society.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Doctor of Social Science Programme in Applied Social Science
courses.learning_outcomes:
By the end of this course, students will be able to understand and learn:

1. Introduction to generative AI in social science research through a foundational understanding of generative AI technologies, with a focus on their application in social science research, including key concepts, trends, and methodologies that are crucial for integrating generative AI into social science research.
2. Critical analysis of trends, strengths, and limitations of using generative AI in social science research.
3. Research skills and ability to formulate research questions and design studies that incorporate generative AI, ensure methodological rigor, and address ethical considerations in AI research.
4. Catalyst for Research Idea Generation to conceptualize and refine new or existing research ideas that leverage generative AI to address current questions in applied social sciences, with a particular focus on applied social science research in frontier technology sectors, policy areas, and decision-making processes.
courses.course_syllabus:
1. Introduction: AI for social science research

2. AI and Research design in social science research

3. Research ethics in Using AI for social science research

4. Use/Limitations of AI in Research plan, process & causation

5. Use/Limitations of AI in Research questions & methods

6. Use/Limitations of AI in Interviews & qualitative methods

7. Use/Limitations of AI for Sampling and structural analysis

8. Field Trip I: AI applications in the public/non-gov sectors

9. Field Trip II: AI applications in the private sectors

10. AI for Qualitative and quantitative data analysis

11. Field Trip III: AI applications in applied social science research

12. AI ethics for Publishing work

13. Final presentation
